The Naranjo-Huff administration: ‘Bringing the TIDE campus-wide’

Sophie Barton, News Editor
September 28, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:08
Instaread

UNCW’s 80th Student Government administration, Naranjo-Huff, is committed to inviting the student body into the conversation, making SGA more visible and listening closely to what Seahawks actually want. The administration outlined its plans for the 2026-27 academic year during the State of the SGA address on Sept. 15 in the Fisher Student Center Clocktower Lounge.

Through their new platform, TIDE — transparency, innovation, development and engagement — Naranjo-Huff hopes to strengthen its connection with students, expand student access to SGA and pursue campus changes based on student feedback.

Opening remarks

Chief of Staff Kadyn Harrington opened the address before introducing Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs Dr. Robert T. Burrus Jr. to the stage.

Burrus expressed his pride in UNCW’s growth as an institution, stating that there are “over 20,500 students here,” and calling UNCW a “first choice for North Carolinians” and “destination university for all kinds of aspiring students.”

Story continues below advertisement

But Burrus followed these comments by ensuring the audience knew one thing: “These students are not just a statistic. You’re not a statistic.”

Burrus also touched on UNCW’s recent achievements, including the proposed medical school. “We have a really exciting opportunity to prepare physicians for the state of North Carolina,” he said. The Cicero Institute projects North Carolina to be short 7,725 doctors by 2030, a shortage UNCW’s proposed medical school aims to help address by expanding physician training in southeastern North Carolina.

He discussed the work set to be done on the medical school this upcoming year and how much they’ve already accomplished, inviting students to come to him for updates. Burrus stated that UNCW is in good financial shape, with a state-provided budget ensuring that the university is able to educate its growing number of students.

Following Burrus’ updates, Harrington invited the next speaker to the stage, new Student Body President Russia Naranjo, to share what she and Vice President Jansen Huff have planned for the 2026-27 academic year.

The Naranjo-Huff administration’s biggest goal for the 2026-27 academic year is to bring SGA closer to the student body. Naranjo made this clear throughout the address, emphasizing how passionate they are about connecting with the student body. This is nothing new for Naranjo, who campaigned on creating a close, personal relationship with Seahawks during her presidential campaign last year.

“We wanted our leadership to be defined not only by what we’ll accomplish together, but by the methods of leadership we choose every single day,” Naranjo said. She made the Naranjo-Huff administration’s mission clear: to encourage SGA to lead with intention and follow through with their goals to reach the student body as closely as they can.

 

Naranjo’s leadership plan: The three P’s

Naranjo explained her leadership plan for SGA this year to help make sure they can make as much difference as possible for Seahawks. She called this the “three P’s:” positivity, productivity and professionalism.

“Positivity is how we approach challenges and how we approach one another, keeping open minds and reaching for what Seahawks want,” Naranjo said. “No idea is too big or too small.” Naranjo made her passion for advocating for the student body clear, emphasizing how much the student body relies on SGA to make a difference in their student experience — something that many students may not be aware of.

Making a tangible difference is a large part of what Naranjo-Huff is committed to. “I don’t want anybody in SGA or anybody at the university to look back at their time spent pursuing their futures, wishing that they had done something else,” she said.

Through her third P, professionalism, Naranjo makes this point clear. She again emphasizes how important connecting with the students is, giving a call to action for her fellow members of the SGA.

“We represent something much larger than ourselves,” Naranjo said. With this year’s student enrollment reaching record-breaking numbers, SGA’s mission to be the voice and vision of the student body is more important than ever. And as Naranjo emphasizes, that responsibility is only going to keep growing.

 

TIDE

That’s why the Naranjo-Huff administration is sticking to their new platform this year, “bringing the TIDE campus-wide.” Through this new initiative, Naranjo-Huff plans to bring SGA closer to the student body than in previous years.

Bringing transparency

Students at UNCW may not be aware of SGA or what they actually do, and some may not even know how to contact them or who is actually representing them. That’s why Naranjo-Huff wants to bring transparency to the forefront of SGA, ensuring that students know who is advocating for them and how they can speak up for themselves.

“Students should never have to wonder what their SGA is doing,” Naranjo said. Through initiatives like Instagram takeovers by the executives and senatorial boards, administrative town halls and their weekly student senate meetings, Naranjo-Huff plans to bring SGA to the forefront of Seahawks’ minds.

“Students will know precisely who represents them,” Naranjo continued. “And more importantly, that when they speak, someone is listening.”

Creating campus change

This year, Naranjo-Huff wants the change SGA works toward to be visible and tangible to students. “We’re continuing our advocacy for things that are going to push the Seahawk experience to become more positive, as Seahawks continue in their journeys here at UNCW,” Naranjo said.

Through their initiatives, Naranjo-Huff wants to make changes that students actually want and give them progress on campus that they can see. She mentioned specific initiatives they are already working toward, such as digital One-Cards, digital signage on Chancellor’s Walk, a dedicated space on campus for commuter students and improvements for outdoor experiences.

She emphasized one idea specifically that they want to bring to campus to give students something new they can hold: a photo booth in the Fisher Student Center or Union.

“This innovative idea could give students, families, visitors, anyone who steps on campus a very unique way to capture a moment,” Naranjo said. “Something to have a physical piece of memorabilia from a UNCW visit.”

Investing in student

When it comes to working closely with the student body, Naranjo-Huff has a plan to “invest directly in student success.” They are working toward creating a round table for registered student organizations (RSOs), allowing organization leaders to meet with SGA and advocate for their needs and ideas directly with their student government.

“That just means having folks from all kinds of RSOs and their leadership come together and talk about similarities, differences and how that leadership experience can be ameliorated,” Naranjo explained.

Engaging the community

“Engagement means ensuring the Student Government Association does not solely operate within the walls of our office, but that we are getting out there,” Naranjo expressed.

Through their various initiatives and new opportunities for students to reach out directly to SGA, Naranjo-Huff plans to bring SGA to the student body, and not the other way around.

“We want to explore how we can celebrate different cultures across campus, possibly partner with other RSOs so we can feel those stronger connections, as well as expand our connection with the greater Wilmington community,” Naranjo said.

Strengthening connections

Last year’s presidential election for SGA brought record student engagement in the SGA process and brought Naranjo and Huff to the positions they hold now. That’s something that Naranjo-Huff is committed to not only continuing but making even stronger.

“Strengthened will be the relationship between Seahawks, the Student Government Association and the community that surrounds our university,” Naranjo said. “No matter what communities you belong to as a Seahawk, SGA’s purpose is to represent you and make sure you have and find the place you want.”

Naranjo and Huff know that the current UNCW experience is not perfect, and there is and will always be room for improvement. They want to know what Seahawks want directly from the students themselves, and more importantly, they want to make it happen. Naranjo reminded her fellow SGA members “progress means very little if the people we serve cannot be connected to it.”

Bringing the TIDE campuswide

“TIDE is more than just a list of projects,” Naranjo said to close. “It’s a commitment to building a Student Government Association that’s visible, accessible, responsive and results-driven.” Naranjo closed by emphasizing the administration’s focus on serving students.

“The state of our Student Government Association is focused,” Naranjo said. “Everyone is very energized and we’re ready to continue to serve, and together, we’re ready to continue and bring the TIDE campuswide.”
